body.statement: Can the average-law fuzzy-prior handle establish, uniformly over \(0\le\gamma\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}\), the comparison \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,\gamma}^\star\le C_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\) for a finite \(C_\alpha\) depending only on \(\alpha\)? Equivalently, can one construct two priors supported almost surely on \(\mathcal Y_{M,\gamma}\), together with an explicit sequential likelihood-ratio or Le Cam deficiency bound, such that their assignment-averaged observed-data mixture laws have total variation at most \(\eta_\alpha\), their \(\tau_W\)-supports are separated by at least \(c_\alpha\mathfrak R_{\alpha,\gamma}^\star\), and rare low-propensity histories enter through their actual mixture probability?
body.justification: This is the genuinely open step needed to compare the convex AIPW rule with every nonlinear, randomized, variable-length observed-data interval.
body.gap: CaiLow2004 obtains all-interval expected-length bounds from Gaussian mixture moduli, and ArmstrongKolesar2018 uses Gaussian convex-class geometry; adaptive randomization requires schedule-supported priors and assignment-averaged sequential likelihood control.
body.consumer: A positive resolution certifies that no schedule-independent NCC interval uniformly beats the implementable rule by more than a constant.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct, uniformly over the drift budget, two priors supported almost surely on the bounded-TV fixed-schedule class whose adaptive observed-law mixtures meet the prescribed total-variation radius and whose target supports are separated by a universal multiple of the optimized borrowing frontier.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen randomization rule may depend arbitrarily and discontinuously on all earlier observed outcomes. Independent or coordinatewise fuzzy perturbations can therefore change later history probabilities, and the average variance envelope alone supplies no likelihood-ratio or deficiency inequality controlling that feedback.
obligation.attempted: The martingale second-moment calculation controls the estimator but not likelihood ratios between schedule mixtures. A direct two-point perturbation only controls realized score variation and does not guarantee the required total-variation bound after adaptive histories are reweighted. The general overlap-measure testing reduction was proved separately, so the missing step is exactly the schedule-supported adaptive fuzzy-prior construction.
obligation.partial_result:
The all-kernel testing step can be completed without any Gaussian or independent-sample approximation: the proved lemma \(\mathrm{lem:mixture\text{-}modulus\text{-}length\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\) gives
\[
\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge
\eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha).
\]
What remains open is the reverse comparison between the optimized AIPW radius and this observed-law modulus, namely the construction, for the arbitrary adaptive design in the frozen assumptions, of TV-admissible schedule-supported priors with separation of order \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,\gamma}^\star\).
